analysis.investment_thesis: Anand Rathi Wealth is a genuinely excellent, capital-light business — D/E of 0.08, ROE of 47%, and net profit CAGR of 31.6% over seven years speak for themselves. However, at P/E 77x and P/B 37.7x, the price demands perfection forever, which is not how I invest.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.08) with OCF positive all 5 years — exactly the financial discipline I respect
Exceptional capital efficiency: ROE 47%, ROCE 59%, operating margin 40% — rare in any sector
Consistent revenue and profit compounding (22% and 31% CAGR) with expanding EBITDA margins
key_risks: Valuation is dangerously stretched at P/E 77x — any growth disappointment will be harshly punished
Promoter holding of 43.11% is below my 55% comfort floor, reducing my conviction in alignment
Wealth management AUM and revenue are highly correlated with equity market cycles — a prolonged bear market will dent growth
red_flags: Other income spiked to INR 105 Cr in FY26 versus near-zero in prior years — needs explanation; may be inflating reported profits
Promoter stake at 43% is below my non-negotiable 55% threshold
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is the kind of asset-light, high-return business I deeply admire — the economics resemble a toll booth on India's growing HNI wealth. Revenue grew from INR 273 Cr in FY21 to INR 1,149 Cr in FY26, profits from INR 45 Cr to INR 397 Cr, and borrowings remain a negligible INR 83 Cr against INR 998 Cr in equity. The business model earns exceptional returns with virtually no capital consumption.

The problem is purely price. P/E 77x on a wealth management business, however excellent, is not a value investor's entry point — it is a momentum investor's price. My sweet spot is 12–20x earnings for quality businesses. At fair value (say, 30–35x given the quality), this stock is worth roughly half the current price. I would watch it carefully and revisit if it corrects to the INR 1,800–2,000 range. Currently, only hold if already owned.
